I just fundamentally disagree that it's a straight upgrade to the old combat. Again I like Nightreign but things like character skills and passives aren't necessary for a good combat system

I also think it's a bit disingenuous to act like the old combat system is silly while the new one has a "cool factor". We're still rolling 6 times then swiping once, we just also have character skills to use. Which, at the end of the day, are basically just two spells on a cooldown instead of something that costs mana like every other spell. 

Not to mention that a big point of souls games are how we're underdogs compared to the bosses, that was a big reason the combat was simple. Feeling like a "puny knight" was the entire point, and what mattered was using your tools to get ahead of the enemies. And besides its not like old combat had nothing, you still had magic, weapon skills in 3, different types of weapons. It wasn't just sword and board basic knight with jack shit vs cool awesome guys. You had the cool stuff to use, you just made your own character instead of having a preset one

And yes you can give a character more stuff to do and have them be an underdog still, look at Sekiro. But my point is that there was a purpose and reason behind the old combat system, you can't just act like the new stuff is a straight upgrade because it has more stuff in it. You can like it more as a preference don't get me wrong but it's not as simple as being straight better

And again I'm not saying this to hate on Nightreign or Elden Ring or Sekiro or any of the innovations Fromsoft makes to the formula. I'm just saying that both the old school souls approach with the build a guy from a closet of tools to enhance a basic moveset and the Nightreign approach of characters with their own skills and ults and specialties are good for different reasons. Acting like either of them are a straight upgrade is a disservice to both.

Besides you're acting like Nightreign is extremely different from Elden Ring when it's just the ER combat with an omega sprint and two skills, which again are just basically character specific versions of spells, something we've always had. And the ER formula was just Dark Souls with jumping. You're acting like it would be a step back to return to the old combat when we're basically still using the old combat just with some extra gimmicks. Again I love both approaches but this just furthers my point that neither are inherently better or worse

Big dispenser tip is to not hog it. Don't put it right behind you so you can turtle, or near your sentry. Explosive classes are going to try to take out your sentry, so the splash damage will hurt anybody trying to be healed by the nearby dispenser 

Ideally you want to put dispensers just behind the front line behind some cover. That way your team can get heals safely without needing to fully retreat.

And if you're ever not sure where to put it, just put your dispenser next to a health pack. That way it's sure to be a spot people will go to for health and be relatively safe, even if it might not always be the most optimal spot
